findings.summary: build_pipeline wires script-stage sealers (configure/acceptance/human_gate/merger) to publish to config.remote_ref, which for an R4 line dispatch is refs/heads/release/<line-id> instead of the audit branch. Since every stage outcome is sealed and pushed, machine parts (.dev-dispatch/, .dd-evidence/) land on the line branch and the seal pushes advance the remote branch past the frozen base, so the merger's pre-push recheck refuses every production line dispatch with RELEASE_HEAD_ADVANCED (and the merger's own seal would stack a machine commit on the stripped release commit). Violates behavior contract 3 (merger pushes the line branch; machine parts never enter it) and contradicts the same file's own publish_ref design (dd_runner.py:336-343) and the testenv drivers' audit_ref wiring (testenv_r4_sample.py:341). The frozen 13/14 probes stayed green only because the testenv sample hand-rolls its sealers and never exercises build_pipeline.

ReceiptReplayer is constructed with remote_ref=config.remote_ref — the release branch for R4 line dispatches — while implement/review seals publish to the audit branch (publish_ref). Generation-restart replay for a line dispatch would verify and force-with-lease-publish the sealed chain against the wrong ref, breaking receipt-chain continuity for g2+ line dispatches even after the script-sealer wiring is fixed.

No test exercises build_pipeline's sealer publish-ref wiring for release-branch dispatches; the R4 acceptance path bypasses build_pipeline with hand-wired audit_ref sealers, which is exactly the coverage gap that let the blocker pass the acceptance suite.
